channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Manufacturing
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Ransomware halts smart-meter production and shipments at three Osaki Electric plants after a VPN login without MFA
item.category: Top Story
item.description: Osaki Electric, Japan’s largest smart-meter maker, confirmed on 17 November that ransomware had encrypted some of its virtual servers. It cut external connections and on 18 November shut down production-related systems at its Saitama Works and at group companies Iwate Osaki Electric and Osaki Platec, suspending production and shipments. The company says the production equipment itself was not encrypted; systems were stopped to keep the infection from spreading. Its 20 November update says the intruder most likely got in on 15 November through a VPN device, by repeated password attempts on an account without multi-factor authentication, some 57 hours before encryption. Technical information believed to be its own has been posted online, and Qilin has listed the company on its leak site. No restart date has been given. Precautionary shutdowns like this are how ransomware usually stops a factory (editorial assessment). - Osaki Electric disclosures of 17–20 Nov 2026, via TipRanks (20 Nov 2026, from the company filing) and BigGo Finance (20 Nov 2026) - Intrusion 15 Nov; encryption 17 Nov; production halted 18 Nov 2026; Qilin listing 19 Nov; no restart date announced

item.title: [Critical] Attackers rooted unpatched Check Point gateways through PHP2Shell, planted backdoors and wiped a VMware host; the root flaw is now in KEV
item.category: Incident — PHP2Shell plus Gaia root flaw CVE-2026-123039 used to backdoor Check Point gateways and wipe a VMware ESXi host (wave 1 from 30 Oct, Israel; wave 2 from 2 Nov, multiple countries); CVE-2026-123039 added to CISA KEV 13 Nov 2026
item.description: Check Point Research said on 12 November that attackers exploited the PHP2Shell flaws on unpatched Check Point Mobile Access portals from 30 October, then used a local flaw (CVE-2026-123039) to become root. They planted backdoors, pivoted to a VMware ESXi host and ran a wiper. The first wave hit Israeli organizations, some destructively; a second wave from 2 November reached several countries without destruction. Attribution is unconfirmed (tooling resembles China-nexus UNC5221). CISA added the root flaw to KEV on 13 November. No OT victim is reported, but these firewalls often sit at the IT/OT boundary and ESXi often hosts HMIs and historians (editorial assessment). - Check Point Research (12 Nov 2026); SecurityWeek (13 Nov 2026); Canadian Centre for Cyber Security AV26-1154 (12 Nov 2026, updated 13 Nov); CISA KEV alert (13 Nov 2026); BleepingComputer (Nov 2026) - Wave 1 from 30 Oct 2026; wave 2 from 2 Nov 2026; research published 12 Nov 2026; KEV addition 13 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] AI-run intrusions took about 150,000 documents from an industrial-automation manufacturer and planted admin accounts at a chip maker, Unit 42 says
item.category: Intrusions — Unit 42 Cairn campaign (CL-STA-1238), Aug–Sep 2026; seven of at least 19 targets in semiconductor and advanced-manufacturing supply chains; report published 12 Nov 2026; China-nexus, moderate confidence
item.description: Palo Alto Networks’ Unit 42 reported on 12 November that an actor it tracks as CL-STA-1238 ran 25 operations against at least 19 organizations in August and September using Cairn, an AI-driven penetration-testing framework, and confirmed access or data theft at 10. Seven targets were in semiconductor and advanced-manufacturing supply chains. At an industrial-automation manufacturer the attackers accessed roughly 150,000 internal documents; at a semiconductor company they brute-forced a production credential shared across accounts on a partner-integration application, then created administrator accounts and a persistent API token. Entry relied on weak and shared passwords, authentication flaws and old CVEs. Unit 42 assesses with moderate confidence that this is China-nexus intelligence collection. No ICS compromise or production outage is reported; design and partner data are the prize (editorial assessment). - Palo Alto Networks Unit 42, 12 Nov 2026 (primary); Security Boulevard Daily OT Security News, 17 Nov 2026 - Activity Aug–Sep 2026; published 12 Nov 2026

item.title: [Critical] CISA and FBI warn of an ongoing threat to internet-connected refrigeration as European supermarket attacks reach at least 11 countries
item.category: Incident — CISA/FBI/HHS/USDA/DOT joint warning (5 Nov 2026) and a second wave of refrigeration attacks across about 11 European countries (1–4 Nov); Belgium says its evidence points to Iran (12 Nov), no formal attribution
item.description: Hackers are tampering with internet-connected refrigeration controllers in European supermarkets, and on 5 November CISA and the FBI warned the threat is ongoing and also reaches healthcare, chemical, transport and cold-storage operations. Hundreds of French stores were hit in October; a second wave on 1–2 November reached about 11 countries, forcing units into continuous heating or defrost. Belgium’s interior minister said on 12 November that evidence points to Iran, short of formal attribution; France has blamed Iran’s IRGC for its October attack, and a pro-Russian claim is unverified. Sekoia says the second wave used a non-public, unauthenticated flaw that renames the controller’s admin account. Cold-storage and process-cooling controllers in food, chemical and pharmaceutical plants face the same risk if reachable from the internet (editorial assessment). - TechCrunch (5 Nov 2026, CISA/FBI joint statement); SentinelOne Labs (3 Nov 2026, updated 4 Nov); Cybersecurity Dive (3 Nov 2026, updated with 4 Nov developments); Unit 42 (6 Nov 2026, exposure counts); Censys (6 Nov 2026, exposure analysis); BleepingComputer (5 Nov 2026); Nextgov (29 Oct 2026); Al Jazeera (4 Nov 2026); CERT-FR CERTFR-2026-ALE-012; The Cyber Express (6 Nov 2026, CISA/FBI/HHS/USDA/DOT advisory summary); Industrial Cyber (6 Nov 2026); Help Net Security (6 Nov 2026); SecurityWeek (6 Nov 2026, hardening guidance); The Hacker News (9 Nov 2026, exposure trend); eBuilder Security (11 Nov 2026, Swedish government and NCSC warning); Arab News/AFP (12 Nov 2026, Belgian statement); Sekoia TDR (10 Nov 2026, second-wave technique) - Attacks overnight 1–2 Nov 2026; Germany, Romania and UK confirmed 4 Nov 2026; CISA/FBI joint warning 5 Nov 2026; French attribution of the October attack 9 Nov 2026; Swedish government warning 10 Nov 2026; Belgian minister points to Iran 12 Nov 2026 — investigations ongoing

item.title: [High] Bloomberg reports that Russia-aligned hackers have tampered with exposed controls at factories since 2024, including a Spanish transformer plant where machinery malfunctioned and caught fire
item.category: Hacktivist sabotage — Bloomberg review of Russia-aligned groups tampering with internet-exposed controls at factories, water systems and other sites since 2024; confirmation varies by case
item.description: Bloomberg News published a review on 27 October of what it calls hundreds of attacks since 2024 by a loose network of Russia-sympathetic hackers on factories, water plants, dams and other sites. In Spain, it reports that machinery making renewable-energy transformers at a factory in Catalonia malfunctioned and caught fire, and that heating and ventilation at two wineries sent temperatures spiking. Meduza’s summary of the full article adds a Los Angeles-area meatpacking plant whose refrigeration was shut off in 2024, causing an ammonia leak and an evacuation. Who confirmed each case is not always stated; the best-confirmed is a December 2024 attack on a Danish waterworks that Denmark attributed to Z-Pentest. The common thread is tampering with internet-reachable HMIs and controllers protected by weak passwords, not advanced exploits (editorial assessment). - Bloomberg News (Ryan Gallagher), 27 Oct 2026 (primary; partly paywalled); Meduza summary, 28 Oct 2026; Danish Defence Intelligence Service attribution, Dec 2025, via AP/SecurityWeek and Euronews - Review published 27 Oct 2026; cases since 2024

item.title: [Medium] ESET documents the first destructive attack by a Belarus-aligned group in Europe, against a Ukrainian manufacturer, and a Sandworm wiper attack built on another group’s access
item.category: Destructive attacks — ESET: a Belarus-aligned group hit a Ukrainian manufacturer; Sandworm wiped a Ukrainian grain logistics firm using access handed over by UAC-0099; no OT impact described
item.description: ESET’s APT Activity Report for April to September 2026, published 28 October, says the Belarus-aligned group FrostyNeighbor carried out a destructive attack on an unnamed Ukrainian manufacturer that plays an important role in the country’s transport sector, the first destructive attack by a Belarus-aligned actor that ESET has documented in Europe. The report gives no date, malware or effect on production. Separately, ESET research of 22 October shows Russia-aligned UAC-0099 breaking into a Ukrainian grain logistics firm by spearphishing in July 2025 and, ESET assesses with high confidence, handing the access to Sandworm, which wiped data that September by pushing SDelete through Active Directory Group Policy. Neither report describes OT targeting. One Group Policy push can wipe engineering and MES servers as easily as office PCs if they share a domain (editorial assessment). - ESET APT Activity Report Q2–Q3 2026, 28 Oct 2026 (primary); ESET Research, MythicRatatoskr, 22 Oct 2026 (primary) - FrostyNeighbor attack undated (report covers Apr–Sep 2026); Sandworm wiping 17 Sep 2025; no OT impact described

item.title: [Medium] Dragos counts 1,266 ransomware attacks on industrial organizations in Q3, up 11%, and found no case of an operator touching a control system
item.category: Research — Dragos Industrial Ransomware Analysis for Q3 2026 (published 16 Nov 2026), covering July–September; Check Point October 2026 statistics (12 Nov 2026) for comparison
item.description: Dragos said on 16 November that ransomware hit 1,266 industrial organizations between July and September 2026, up 11% on the second quarter, while the number of brands claiming industrial victims jumped from 70 to 99. Manufacturing took 876 cases (69%), led by construction, equipment and food and beverage makers, with automotive at 53; next came the ICS ecosystem of integrators, engineering firms and equipment makers (116) and transport and logistics (105); oil and gas logged 47. Qilin and The Gentlemen drove 29% of the total. Dragos saw no Q3 case of a ransomware operator manipulating a control system: production stopped because the IT, ERP and virtualization layers plants rely on went down, as when Fairlife reportedly halted all four of its US plants for about 11 days. Entry came through edge devices and enterprise applications exploited within days of disclosure, and through stolen VPN and firewall credentials. Check Point separately counted a record 1,063 claimed victims across all sectors in October. - Dragos (16 Nov 2026); Australian Cyber Security Magazine (17 Nov 2026); Check Point Research October 2026 statistics, via iTWire (12 Nov 2026) - Published 16 Nov 2026; data covers July–September 2026

item.title: [Medium] Intel 471: manufacturing was the sector most targeted by ransomware groups and access brokers from January to October
item.category: Research — Intel 471, “Aerospace to chemicals: why manufacturers are easy targets for access brokers” (18 Nov 2026), covering January–October 2026
item.description: Intel 471 said on 18 November that manufacturing was the sector most targeted by ransomware and extortion groups between January and October 2026, with 1,379 claimed victims, 16.8% of all the victims it tracked. Initial access brokers advertised access affecting 172 manufacturing entities, about 10% of all accesses offered for sale in the period. Perimeter remote access dominated those listings, with VPN access alone making up 28.5%. Intel 471 names Qilin, The Gentlemen and Akira among the groups most active against manufacturers and automotive supply chains. The figures come from Intel 471’s own tracking of leak sites and criminal forums and have not been independently verified. For plants, the practical point is that a working VPN login may already be on sale before anyone uses it (editorial assessment). - Intel 471 (18 Nov 2026); Industrial Cyber coverage (Nov 2026) - Published 18 Nov 2026; data covers January–October 2026

item.title: [Medium] Trellix: ransomware leak-site posts naming industrial firms rose about 51% in a quarter, and manufacturing made up about two-thirds
item.category: Research — Trellix OT Threat Report, November 2026 (page updated 12 Nov 2026), covering April–September 2026
item.description: Trellix’s November 2026 OT threat report, covering April to September 2026, counts about 1,500 ransomware leak-site posts naming organizations in manufacturing, construction, transportation and warehousing, mining and oil and gas extraction, and utilities, up 50.8% quarter on quarter. Manufacturing accounted for about two-thirds of those posts and utilities for under 2%; The Gentlemen and Qilin each made about 16% of them. Manufacturing also produced 49.3% of Trellix’s OT-related product telemetry, a measure of detection activity rather than confirmed compromise. Trellix says the enterprise edge exploitation it observed did not establish a path into ICS networks. The pattern matches Dragos and Intel 471: plants are hit through business IT and stop when that IT stops (editorial assessment). - Trellix Advanced Research Center, OT Threat Report November 2026 - Page updated 12 Nov 2026; data covers April–September 2026

item.title: [Medium] FBI warns that the ARTEX AI attack framework is reaching privileged access in under three hours, with manufacturing among its targets
item.category: Government alert — FBI FLASH-20261113-001 (13 Nov 2026) on misuse of the ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework; manufacturing and semiconductor among the targeted sectors
item.description: The FBI issued a FLASH alert on 13 November about ARTEX, an open-source, AI-driven penetration-testing framework that multiple malicious actors have used since at least August 2026 to automate intrusions from reconnaissance to data theft. Some intrusions reached privileged access in under three hours. The FBI lists manufacturing, semiconductor, energy, telecommunications and other sectors as targets and counts more than 1,600 exposed ARTEX consoles as of early November; the original repository was removed in October, but forks and a commercial version persist. Its examples include attacks on South Korean financial institutions and the ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply-chain compromise, which produced sign-in attempts against more than 2,250 downstream tenants. No controller compromise or OT outage is described. Faster intrusions shrink the time between a missed patch and a stopped plant (editorial assessment). - FBI FLASH-20261113-001, 13 Nov 2026 (primary, TLP:CLEAR); Security Boulevard Daily OT Security News, 17 Nov 2026 - Issued 13 Nov 2026; malicious use since Aug 2026

item.title: [Medium] DHS tells Congress Iran-backed hackers have stepped up attacks on US water, energy and transport since February, while officials rule out hacking in last week’s outages
item.category: Government threat assessment — DHS Secretary’s written testimony to the House Homeland Security Committee (18 Nov 2026); DNI and DHS tell the same hearing recent US outages were not cyberattacks
item.description: In written testimony for a House Homeland Security Committee hearing on 18 November, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said Iranian state-sponsored groups and pro-Iranian criminals have targeted US critical infrastructure since the conflict with Iran began in February, with transportation, healthcare, water, energy and financial services increasingly in their sights. He described the attacks so far as mostly localized, low-damage disruptions of poorly secured industrial control systems, but warned that weak systems and poor cyber hygiene could have devastating consequences. At the same hearing the Director of National Intelligence and DHS said they found no evidence that hackers caused last week’s Microsoft 365 outage, the nationwide FAA ground stop or other recent disruptions, which officials tie to software defects and upgrade failures. Separately, AttackIQ research released on 17 November describes Iranian groups handing network access to one another, with long-running espionage access later passed to teams pursuing destructive goals, sometimes disguised as ransomware or hacktivism, often reaching targets through contractors and suppliers. For OT owners, the official US view now matches France’s: Iran is going after the weakest exposed controllers. - Jerusalem Post (18 Nov 2026, Mullin written testimony); Report.az (18 Nov 2026); Bloomberg (18 Nov 2026); Federal News Network (18 Nov 2026, outages not a coordinated attack); Washington Examiner (18 Nov 2026, hearing); AttackIQ “Weighing Cyber Power”, via Water Online (17 Nov 2026) - Testimony and hearing 18 Nov 2026; AttackIQ research 17 Nov 2026

item.title: [Medium] Lumen exposes the single-use relay chains Volt Typhoon uses to reach critical-infrastructure targets, and ties the group to zero-days in SD-WAN and IT management platforms
item.category: Nation-state pre-positioning — Lumen Black Lotus Labs on Volt Typhoon’s “Silent Train” relay network and management-platform zero-days; cross-sector, manufacturing not among the named sectors
item.description: Lumen’s Black Lotus Labs reported on 28 October that Volt Typhoon, the China state-linked group, has since about November 2023 used “Silent Train”: rotating, single-use chains of compromised home and small-office routers, IoT devices and enterprise equipment, often rebuilt in under two minutes, to reach targets and exploit management and control-plane platforms. Lumen ties the group to zero-days in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN (CVE-2026-20127, CVSS v3.1 10.0 per Cisco, in KEV since 25 February), VeloCloud Orchestrator (CVE-2026-16812, in KEV since 27 July) and N-able N-central (CVE-2025-8875 and -8876), to a Versa Director campaign with no CVE given, and probably to Quest KACE. Lumen names water, energy, rail, maritime, aviation and other transportation, and emergency services among critical-infrastructure targets, alongside telecoms, government, defence contractors and managed-service providers; it names no victim and describes no OT intrusion. Manufacturing is not a named sector, but defence suppliers and multi-site manufacturers run the same SD-WAN orchestrators and IT management tools (cross-sector item; editorial assessment). - Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 28 Oct 2026 (primary); CyberScoop and Zero Day, 28 Oct 2026; KEV dates via CIRCL - Report published 28 Oct 2026; activity since about Nov 2023; no OT intrusion described

item.title: [Critical] PHP2Shell attacks rooted about two dozen Palo Alto firewalls, and Siemens, Schneider and ABB now list grid-control, DCS and RTU products, several with no fix
item.category: Active exploitation — PHP2Shell chained with a Linux kernel flaw to root exposed PAN-OS firewalls, 23–24 Oct; OT vendor advisories 28–30 Oct; Siemens adds metering gateways 16 Nov
item.description: Palo Alto’s Unit 42 verified that a suspected China-nexus actor chained the PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) with Linux kernel bug CVE-2026-46300 to root about two dozen internet-exposed PAN-OS firewalls on 23–24 October and steal Active Directory credentials. Siemens (Spectrum Power, AMIS TS and, since 16 November, WTV676/WTV776 metering gateways), Schneider (a Foxboro DCS server) and ABB (Netcontrol RTUs, ASPECT gateways) now list affected products, several unfixed. None is reported exploited and no OT operator is named: treat it as an IT-to-OT boundary warning. - Unit 42 (updated 29 Oct 2026); Palo Alto Networks advisory for CVE-2026-109618 (updated 29 Oct 2026); The Record (29 Oct 2026) and Infosecurity Magazine (30 Oct 2026), citing Dream; CISA KEV catalog (30 Oct 2026 release); Siemens SSA-166980 V1.4 (16 Nov 2026, WTV676/WTV776 added; V1.2 29 Oct 2026), SSA-566512 V1.1 (28 Oct 2026), SSA-019113 and SSA-082556; Schneider Electric SESB-2026-295-01 v3.2.0 (30 Oct 2026); ABB Netcontrol and Arctic advisories (30 Oct 2026), ASPECT advisory (29 Oct 2026) and APROL SA26P015 (23 Oct 2026); CERT@VDE VDE-2026-127 and VDE-2026-137 - Root compromises 23–24 Oct 2026, verified by Unit 42 29 Oct 2026; KEV additions 26 and 28 Oct 2026; Siemens, Schneider and ABB updates 28–30 Oct 2026; Siemens metering gateways added 16 Nov 2026

item.title: [Critical] A CVSS 9.8 Brotli flaw reaches more than a dozen Siemens HMI, SCADA and engineering products, and most have no fix yet
item.category: Advisory — Siemens SSA-242944 (10 Nov 2026), republished by CISA as ICSA-26-321-03 (17 Nov 2026): Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497 (CVSS v3.1 9.8) in SIMATIC WinCC, WinCC OA, Braumat, Sistar, TIA Administrator, UMC and more; most products unfixed
item.description: Siemens advisory SSA-242944, republished by CISA on 17 November as ICSA-26-321-03, covers CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in Google’s Brotli decoder (versions 1.0.3 to 1.2.0) linked to the Node.js “Node2Shell” fixes of 21 October. A remote, unauthenticated attacker sending a crafted Brotli-compressed stream could crash the service, leak memory or possibly run code; CVSS v3.1 is 9.8. Fixes exist only for SIMATIC Braumat and Sistar (V8.2 Update 5) and WinCC OA V3.20 (P17.1). WinCC V7/V8, WinCC Runtime Professional, the WinCC Unified family, WinCC OA V3.21, TIA Administrator, User Management Component and COMOS Walkinside have no fix yet, and the SIMATIC Profiling Tool will get none. SecurityWeek reports Node2Shell exploitation attempts in general, but none aimed at Siemens products. - Siemens ProductCERT SSA-242944, 10 Nov 2026 (primary); CISA ICSA-26-321-03, 17 Nov 2026, via DefCon Level; SecurityWeek ICS Patch Tuesday, Nov 2026 - Siemens advisory 10 Nov; CISA republication 17 Nov 2026; Siemens preparing further fixes

item.title: [High] A vCenter authentication bypass was exploited as a zero-day for two months before Broadcom’s 19 November patch; vCenter 7.0 gets no fix
item.category: Active exploitation — VMware vCenter authentication bypass CVE-2026-123890 (CVSS 9.8) exploited as a zero-day for more than two months by a suspected China-linked group, per Mandiant; Broadcom fix released 19 Nov 2026; no public fix for vCenter 7.0
item.description: Broadcom patched CVE-2026-123890 on 19 November, a critical flaw in vCenter’s directory service that lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker obtain an administrator session. Google’s Mandiant, which reported the bug, says a suspected China-linked espionage group it tracks as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221, also called Warp Panda) exploited it for more than two months beforehand. In the incidents Mandiant investigated, the group got in through a BeyondTrust Remote Support flaw, moved to Linux appliances, attacked vCenter in early September with a custom tool called Bonesaw, stole SAML signing material and the vCenter master key, created an SSO admin account, forged tokens and moved on to ESXi hosts. Fixes are in vCenter 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200 and 8.0 U3m; end-of-life vCenter 7.0 has no public patch. No victims or sectors are named. Many plants run HMIs, historians and engineering workstations as virtual machines, so whoever controls vCenter controls those hosts (editorial assessment). - SecurityWeek (19 Nov 2026, citing Broadcom, Google Threat Intelligence/Mandiant and Mandiant CTO Charles Carmakal); CISA KEV alert (20 Nov 2026); The Hacker News (20–21 Nov 2026) - Added to CISA KEV 20 Nov 2026; patched 19 Nov 2026; exploited from at least early Sep 2026

item.title: [High] Java4Shell exploitation attempts begin, and Siemens tells customers to take Industrial Edge Management offline until patched
item.category: Advisory — OpenJDK “Java4Shell” memory-corruption flaw CVE-2026-114938 (disclosed and patched 17 Nov 2026); exploitation attempts seen 18–19 Nov 2026; Siemens SSA-272816 lists three Industrial Edge Management products
item.description: Probing for Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a memory-corruption bug in how OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later decode Base64 data, started within two days of its 17 November disclosure. GreyNoise counted more than 150 matching requests from five addresses by early 19 November and Previdian logged nine attempts from six addresses; none is confirmed to have succeeded. Exploitation needs a recent Intel or AMD x86-64 processor with AVX-512 VBMI, and researchers at Calif showed unauthenticated code execution against default Jira, Confluence, Jenkins and Keycloak setups, each with a tailored chain. For OT teams the key item is Siemens advisory SSA-272816: three Industrial Edge Management products are affected, fixes are in progress, and Siemens recommends taking those instances offline until they are patched. Cisco lists more than a dozen products with no fix yet, and Atlassian Data Center products are also unpatched. - SecurityWeek (19 Nov 2026, citing Calif, GreyNoise, WatchTowr, Cloudflare, Previdian, Siemens SSA-272816, Cisco and Atlassian); The Record (18 Nov 2026, CISA alert) - Disclosed and patched 17 Nov 2026; exploitation attempts 18–19 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Attackers root clustered Cisco Expressway gateways soon after a public exploit, and CISA adds the flaw to KEV
item.category: Active exploitation — Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8), clustered Expressway Core/Edge; exploited after a public PoC (reported by F6); added to CISA KEV 20 Nov 2026; fixed in X15.5.20
item.description: Security firm F6 says attackers exploited CVE-2026-76466, a critical flaw in clustered Cisco Expressway Core and Edge deployments, shortly after proof-of-concept code appeared on GitHub. They broke into two internet-facing Expressway nodes at an unnamed Russian organization, moved to two more cluster nodes inside the network, and gained root. From there they ran Python scripts, which F6 says show signs of AI-assisted writing, to scan for SMB shares, SQL Server and WinRM hosts and to search GitLab for credentials. CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog on 20 November alongside the vCenter zero-day. Cisco disclosed and fixed it on 21 October; there is no workaround. No OT victim is reported, but Expressway is a perimeter gateway that often bridges outside callers into internal networks, so an exposed, unpatched cluster is a foothold close to plant-side systems (editorial assessment). - Security Affairs (21 Nov 2026, CISA KEV additions of 20 Nov); SecurityWeek (Nov 2026, citing F6); Security Affairs (20 Nov 2026, F6 findings) - Added to CISA KEV 20 Nov 2026; exploitation reported 18–20 Nov 2026; patched 21 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] N-able ships Hotfix 3 for 17 more N-central flaws after attackers planted miners on servers already running Hotfix 2
item.category: Active exploitation — N-able N-central: 4EverAble2Shell exploited to plant miners (13 Nov 2026); N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 3 fixes 17 more CVEs and removes the Legacy API (16–17 Nov 2026); separate breach of N-able’s hosted Mail Assure/SpamExperts cloud disclosed 20 Nov 2026
item.description: N-able released N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 3 on 16 November, which it calls a critical security update. It fixes 17 new CVEs, including authentication bypasses, missing authorization checks, path traversal leading to code execution and a syslog injection that runs commands as root, and it removes the Legacy API option that the actively exploited 4EverAble2Shell chain depends on. On-premises servers need the upgrade now; hosted servers update automatically, but every customer must also upgrade Agents and Probes, which N-able warns can otherwise be impersonated. The fix follows Huntback’s 13 November finding of cryptocurrency miners on 21 N-central servers, 19 of them on Hotfix 2. Remote control and Intune integration stay blocked for now. Separately, N-able said on 20 November that attackers reached a server in its hosted Mail Assure and SpamExperts email-filtering cloud, forcing it to take the management portal and APIs offline; it says mail flow continued, it has found no access to customer data, and the breach is unrelated to N-central. Many integrators manage plant-side Windows hosts through RMM tools, and a miner today can be a hands-on intruder tomorrow (editorial assessment). - BleepingComputer (20 Nov 2026, Mail Assure/SpamExperts breach); The Hacker News (17 Nov 2026, Hotfix 3, citing N-able release notes of 16 Nov); The Hacker News (13 Nov 2026, citing Huntback and Previdian); The Hacker News (12 Nov 2026, new chains); SecurityWeek (13 Nov 2026); Tenable (10 Nov 2026) - Mail Assure breach disclosed 20 Nov 2026; Hotfix 3 released 16 Nov 2026; exploitation reported 13 Nov 2026; Able2Shell disclosed 9 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Siemens: an NTLM relay flaw in PCS 7, WinCC and Process Historian will not be fixed in older versions, and opening a WinCC graphics file can run code
item.category: Advisories — Siemens SSA-970803 (NTLM relay, CVE-2026-58114, CVSS v3.1 7.5) and SSA-979641 (WinCC Graphics Designer, CVE-2026-59082, CVSS 7.8), 10 Nov 2026; republished by CISA as ICSA-26-321-08 and ICSA-26-321-09, 17 Nov 2026
item.description: Two Siemens advisories republished by CISA on 17 November reach the core of many process and discrete plants. CVE-2026-58114 (CVSS v3.1 7.5) lets an unauthenticated attacker in a machine-in-the-middle position relay NTLM authentication and impersonate a user, for example against the SQL server WinCC uses. It affects SIMATIC PCS 7 V9.1, Batch V9.1, Information Server and Process Historian 2020 and 2022, for which no fix is planned, and WinCC V7.5 to V8.1 and WinCC Runtime Professional V17 to V21, which have no fix yet. Separately, CVE-2026-59082 (CVSS 7.8) in the WinCC Graphics Designer can run code when a user opens a malicious file; there is no fix for V7.5, V8.0 or V8.1. Neither flaw is reported exploited. - Siemens ProductCERT SSA-970803 and SSA-979641, 10 Nov 2026 (primary); CISA ICSA-26-321-08 and ICSA-26-321-09, 17 Nov 2026, via DefCon Level; SecurityWeek ICS Patch Tuesday, Nov 2026 - Siemens advisories 10 Nov; CISA republication 17 Nov 2026; Siemens preparing fixes for current WinCC versions

item.title: [High] Mitsubishi Electric fixes an authentication bypass in ICONICS GENESIS SCADA software, but MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz will get no fix
item.category: Vendor advisory — Mitsubishi Electric 2026-006, ICONICS GENESIS64 / GENESIS SCADA and HMI suite; CVSS v4.0 up to 9.4
item.description: Mitsubishi Electric’s advisory 2026-006, published 15 October, covers flaws across the ICONICS GENESIS64 and GENESIS SCADA and HMI suite. CVE-2026-16436 (CVSS v4.0 9.2) is an authentication bypass: a shared, fixed challenge-response can unlock any user account, although a remote attacker must first obtain that response. CVE-2026-16438 (v4.0 9.4) concerns default DCOM permissions granted to the administrator account, CVE-2026-16437 (v4.0 7.1) lets an administrator read or write the challenge-response file, and the older libwebp flaw CVE-2023-4863 (v4.0 9.3) affects ICONICS Suite 10.97 to 10.97.2 if a local administrator imports a crafted file. Affected are GENESIS 11.03 and earlier; GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI and IoTWorX 10.97.3 and earlier; and all versions of MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz. Fixes are ICONICS Suite and IoTWorX 10.98, GENESIS 11.04 and, for libwebp, ICONICS Suite 10.97.3; MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz will not be fixed. CISA republished the advisory on 27 October as ICSA-26-300-02, listing CVSS v3.1 scores of 9.1 for CVE-2026-16438, 8.1 for CVE-2026-16436, 6.4 for CVE-2026-16437 and 8.2 for CVE-2023-4863. None of the ICONICS-specific flaws is in KEV; the bundled libwebp flaw CVE-2023-4863 has been in KEV since 13 September 2023 from browser exploitation. No exploitation of ICONICS products is reported. GENESIS64 and Hyper Historian commonly run plant HMIs and historians (editorial assessment). - Mitsubishi Electric PSIRT advisory 2026-006, 15 Oct 2026 (primary); CISA ICSA-26-300-02, 27 Oct 2026; CISA KEV entry for CVE-2023-4863 (13 Sep 2023, via CIRCL) - Published 15 Oct 2026; republished by CISA 27 Oct 2026; not exploited

item.title: [Medium] Moxa fixes a remote-access client that can be tricked into trusting a fake server, and leaves an end-of-life cellular gateway with static keys unfixed
item.category: Vendor advisories — Moxa MRC Client (Remote Connect) CVE-2026-111459; end-of-life OnCell G3150A-LTE CVE-2026-111460 / -111461, no fix
item.description: Moxa published two advisories on 27 October. CVE-2026-111459 (Moxa CVSS v4.0 7.6) affects MRC Client 1.0.0 to 4.2.0, the OpenVPN-based client for Moxa Remote Connect: it accepts a server-supplied configuration without proper certificate validation, so an attacker in the network path could impersonate the server. Version 4.2.2, available through Moxa support, fixes it. The OnCell G3150A-LTE cellular gateway has static HTTPS and CA private keys in its firmware (CVE-2026-111460, 7.7) and a command injection in its SMS-based upgrade function (CVE-2026-111461, 7.5); the product is end-of-life and will not be fixed, so Moxa advises resetting the device to regenerate its keys and keeping SMS disabled. No exploitation is reported. Remote-access clients and cellular gateways like these are common ways for machine builders and integrators to reach equipment on the plant floor (editorial assessment). - Moxa security advisories MPSA-269510 and MPSA-261250, 27 Oct 2026 (primary) - Published 27 Oct 2026; OnCell G3150A-LTE end-of-life, no fix

item.title: [Info] CISA’s new four-year strategy names OT security and consequence-based prioritisation, with a review of its core services due to start within 60 days
item.category: Strategy — “CISA 2030: Defend, Harden, Prevail”; OT security named as an objective
item.description: CISA released “CISA 2030: Defend, Harden, Prevail” on 26 October. Under its Defend pillar the agency lists protecting operational technology, including modernising OT environments and improving asset visibility and anomaly detection, alongside supply-chain integrity. It says it will move away from all-hazards approaches toward risk-informed, consequence-based analysis, and it supports a national risk register. CISA will begin a review of its core services within 60 days, deliver an implementation plan with metrics within 180 days and report progress after a year. The strategy creates no new legal obligations, and analysts quoted by GovInfoSecurity questioned whether the agency can deliver it after losing about a third of its staff. - CISA 2030 strategy, 26 Oct 2026 (primary), as reported by Cybersecurity Dive and CyberScoop, 26 Oct 2026; GovInfoSecurity - Core-services review to begin within 60 days; implementation plan within 180 days
